title: Life Processes
seo_title: Life Processes Class 10 Science Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 5)
standard_text: Life processes: 'living being', basic concept of nutrition, respiration, transport and excretion in plants and animals.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 10 Science worksheets for NCERT Chapter 5: nutrition, photosynthesis, digestion, respiration, the heart and blood, transport in plants and excretion. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Nutrition, respiration, transport and excretion keep us alive.
body_html:
How to think about it

Living things need energy and materials. Plants make food by photosynthesis (CO₂ + water → glucose + O₂ with sunlight and chlorophyll); animals take in food and digest it with enzymes such as amylase, pepsin, trypsin and lipase. Respiration releases energy from glucose: with oxygen it gives CO₂ and water; without oxygen yeast makes ethanol and muscles make lactic acid.

Humans have double circulation: the four-chambered heart pumps blood to the lungs and to the body. Plants move water in xylem and food in phloem. Kidneys filter blood in nephrons to make urine.

Example

Where is protein digestion started?

pepsin works in acid

Answer: the stomach

Example

Products of anaerobic respiration in yeast?

pyruvate without oxygen

Answer: ethanol and carbon dioxide

Common mistakes

  • Saying plants do not respire.
  • Mixing up xylem (water) and phloem (food).
  • Thinking the pulmonary vein carries deoxygenated blood.

faq.q: Why is diffusion not enough for oxygen in large animals?
faq.a: Diffusion is too slow over long distances, so large animals need lungs and a circulatory system.

faq.q: What is the role of the nephron?
faq.a: It filters the blood, reabsorbs useful substances and makes urine from the waste.

items.q: What is the mode of nutrition of human beings?
items.e: human beings: holozoic.

items.q: Where is bile secreted?
items.e: Bile is secreted in the liver.

items.q: Which blood vessel carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart?
items.e: It is a vein that carries oxygenated blood.

items.q: Why is the small intestine very long?
c: to give enough time and surface for digestion and absorption
items.e: Herbivores eating grass have a longer small intestine than carnivores.

items.q: What does salivary amylase act on?
c: nothing directly: it emulsifies fats into small droplets
nothing directly: it makes the medium acidic for pepsin
items.e: Salivary amylase (from the mouth) acts on starch into sugar.

items.q: What is the purpose of making urine?
c: removing harmful nitrogenous waste such as urea from the blood
items.e: Urine also removes extra water and salts.

items.q: What is translocation?
c: the transport of food (sucrose) in the phloem
items.e: It uses energy from ATP.

items.q: What is the mode of nutrition of bread mould and mushrooms?
items.e: bread mould and mushrooms: saprotrophic.

items.q: Where is lipase secreted?
items.e: Lipase is secreted in the pancreas.

items.q: What are the three events in photosynthesis?
c: absorbing light, splitting water and reducing CO₂ to carbohydrate
breathing in, breathing out and resting
items.e: They need not happen one right after another.

items.q: Where is salivary amylase secreted?
items.e: Salivary amylase is secreted in the mouth.

items.q: How do plants get rid of some waste products?
c: they store them in leaves that fall, as resins and gums, or in vacuoles
items.e: Plants also lose oxygen and water vapour through stomata.

items.q: What is selective reabsorption in the kidney?
c: useful substances such as glucose and some water are taken back into the blood
items.e: It happens in the tubule of the nephron.

items.q: What does pepsin act on?
c: nothing directly: it emulsifies fats into small droplets
nothing directly: it makes the medium acidic for pepsin
items.e: Pepsin (from the stomach) acts on proteins.

items.q: Where is pepsin secreted?
items.e: Pepsin is secreted in the stomach.

items.q: Why do the walls of the left ventricle need to be thick?
c: it pumps blood to all parts of the body at high pressure
it receives blood from the lungs
items.e: The right ventricle pumps only to the lungs.

items.q: What does bile act on?
c: nothing directly: it makes the medium acidic for pepsin
nothing directly: it emulsifies fats into small droplets
items.e: Bile (from the liver) acts on nothing directly: it emulsifies fats into small droplets.

items.q: What is double circulation?
c: blood passes through the heart twice in each cycle of the body
blood flows in two directions at once
items.e: Once to the lungs and once to the body.

items.q: Where is trypsin secreted?
items.e: Trypsin is secreted in the pancreas.

items.q: What is the mode of nutrition of green plants?
items.e: green plants: autotrophic.

items.q: What is the function of rings of cartilage in the trachea?
c: changing the volume of the chest cavity during breathing
stopping the air passage from collapsing
items.e: Rings of cartilage in the trachea: stopping the air passage from collapsing.

items.q: What is the function of nephron?
c: carrying oxygen in red blood cells
carrying food from leaves to other parts of the plant
filtering blood to remove waste as urine
carrying digested fat and draining excess tissue fluid back into the blood
items.e: Nephron: filtering blood to remove waste as urine.

items.q: What is the function of villi in the small intestine?
c: increasing the surface area for absorbing digested food
bringing deoxygenated blood from the body to the heart
carrying water and minerals from roots to leaves
items.e: Villi in the small intestine: increasing the surface area for absorbing digested food.

items.q: What is the function of capillaries?
c: exchanging materials between blood and cells through thin walls
carrying air from the nose and throat to the lungs
changing the volume of the chest cavity during breathing
items.e: Capillaries: exchanging materials between blood and cells through thin walls.

items.q: What is the function of Bowman's capsule?
c: carrying food from leaves to other parts of the plant
collecting the filtrate from the glomerulus
receiving deoxygenated blood from the body
items.e: Bowman's capsule: collecting the filtrate from the glomerulus.

items.q: Which part of the body or plant does this job: carrying digested fat and draining excess tissue fluid back into the blood?
items.e: Lymph: carrying digested fat and draining excess tissue fluid back into the blood.

items.q: Which part of the body or plant does this job: carrying blood away from the heart at high pressure?
c: rings of cartilage in the trachea
items.e: Arteries: carrying blood away from the heart at high pressure.

items.q: Which part of the body or plant does this job: carrying water and minerals from roots to leaves?
items.e: Xylem: carrying water and minerals from roots to leaves.

items.q: What is the function of white blood cells?
c: exchanging materials between blood and cells through thin walls
carrying water and minerals from roots to leaves
items.e: White blood cells: fighting infection.

items.q: What is the function of glomerulus?
c: bringing blood back to the heart
stopping the air passage from collapsing
a cluster of capillaries where blood is filtered in the kidney
items.e: Glomerulus: a cluster of capillaries where blood is filtered in the kidney.

items.q: What is the function of arteries?
c: carrying digested fat and draining excess tissue fluid back into the blood
carrying blood away from the heart at high pressure
controlling the removal of undigested waste
making pancreatic juice with trypsin and lipase
items.e: Arteries: carrying blood away from the heart at high pressure.

items.q: Which part of the body or plant does this job: increasing the surface area for absorbing digested food?
items.e: Villi in the small intestine: increasing the surface area for absorbing digested food.

items.q: Which part of the body or plant does this job: exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide in the lungs?
items.e: Alveoli: exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide in the lungs.

items.q: Which part of the body or plant does this job: making saliva with salivary amylase?
items.e: Salivary glands: making saliva with salivary amylase.

items.q: What is the function of the large intestine?
c: pumping oxygenated blood to the whole body
absorbing extra water from undigested food
closing the windpipe when we swallow food
items.e: The large intestine: absorbing extra water from undigested food.

items.q: Which part of the body or plant does this job: filtering blood to remove waste as urine?
items.e: Nephron: filtering blood to remove waste as urine.

items.q: Which part of the body or plant does this job: closing the windpipe when we swallow food?
items.e: The epiglottis: closing the windpipe when we swallow food.

items.q: What is the function of the pancreas?
c: making pancreatic juice with trypsin and lipase
collecting the filtrate from the glomerulus
receiving deoxygenated blood from the body
items.e: The pancreas: making pancreatic juice with trypsin and lipase.

items.q: What is the function of the diaphragm?
c: changing the volume of the chest cavity during breathing
exchange of gases and loss of water vapour in leaves
items.e: The diaphragm: changing the volume of the chest cavity during breathing.

items.q: What is the function of phloem?
c: bringing blood back to the heart
filtering blood to remove waste as urine
controlling the removal of undigested waste
carrying food from leaves to other parts of the plant
items.e: Phloem: carrying food from leaves to other parts of the plant.

items.q: What is the function of salivary glands?
c: carrying urine out of the body
carrying oxygen in red blood cells
items.e: Salivary glands: making saliva with salivary amylase.

items.q: Which part of the body or plant does this job: carrying oxygenated blood from the heart to the body?
items.e: The aorta: carrying oxygenated blood from the heart to the body.

items.q: How many chambers does the heart of fish have?
items.e: Fish 2, amphibians and most reptiles 3, birds and mammals 4 (complete separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood).

items.q: How many chambers does the heart of frogs (amphibians) have?
items.e: Fish 2, amphibians and most reptiles 3, birds and mammals 4 (complete separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood).

items.q: How many chambers does the heart of crocodiles have?
items.e: Fish 2, amphibians and most reptiles 3, birds and mammals 4 (complete separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood).

items.q: What is the function of the liver?
c: carrying blood away from the heart at high pressure
carrying oxygenated blood from the heart to the body
helping blood to clot at a wound
items.e: The liver: making bile.

items.q: What happens to the energy released in respiration?
c: it is stored as ATP for use by the cell
items.e: ATP is the energy currency of the cell.

items.q: Which part of the body or plant does this job: receiving deoxygenated blood from the body?
items.e: The right atrium: receiving deoxygenated blood from the body.

items.q: What is the function of the trachea?
c: pumping oxygenated blood to the whole body
carrying air from the nose and throat to the lungs
making pancreatic juice with trypsin and lipase
items.e: The trachea: carrying air from the nose and throat to the lungs.

items.q: What is the role of the lungs in the exchange of gases?
c: alveoli give a large surface where oxygen enters and CO₂ leaves the blood
items.e: The alveoli are close to many capillaries.

items.q: Which part of a plant cell contains chlorophyll?
items.e: Chloroplasts are mainly in leaf cells.

items.q: Why do desert plants open their stomata at night?
c: to reduce water loss; they store CO₂ as an acid and use it in the day
items.e: This is how cacti survive.

items.q: How many chambers does the heart of humans have?
items.e: Fish 2, amphibians and most reptiles 3, birds and mammals 4 (complete separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood).

items.q: Which part of the body or plant does this job: carrying oxygen in red blood cells?
items.e: Haemoglobin: carrying oxygen in red blood cells.

items.q: Why does the stomach make hydrochloric acid?
c: to make the medium acidic so pepsin can work and to kill germs
items.e: Too much acid causes acidity.

items.q: How many chambers does the heart of most reptiles have?
items.e: Fish 2, amphibians and most reptiles 3, birds and mammals 4 (complete separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood).

items.q: What is formed from pyruvate in muscle cells short of oxygen?
c: carbon dioxide, water and a lot of energy
pyruvate (a 3-carbon molecule) and a little energy
items.e: Glucose → pyruvate in the cytoplasm; then ethanol + CO₂ (yeast), lactic acid (muscles), or CO₂ + water in mitochondria.

items.q: What is formed from pyruvate in mitochondria with oxygen?
c: pyruvate (a 3-carbon molecule) and a little energy
carbon dioxide, water and a lot of energy
items.e: Glucose → pyruvate in the cytoplasm; then ethanol + CO₂ (yeast), lactic acid (muscles), or CO₂ + water in mitochondria.

items.q: What is formed from glucose in the cytoplasm of all cells?
c: pyruvate (a 3-carbon molecule) and a little energy
carbon dioxide, water and a lot of energy
items.e: Glucose → pyruvate in the cytoplasm; then ethanol + CO₂ (yeast), lactic acid (muscles), or CO₂ + water in mitochondria.

items.q: Which part of the body or plant does this job: changing the volume of the chest cavity during breathing?
items.e: The diaphragm: changing the volume of the chest cavity during breathing.

items.q: Why do red blood cells lack a nucleus in mammals?
c: more space for haemoglobin to carry oxygen
items.e: They are disc-shaped too.

items.q: What is the function of the urethra?
c: exchange of gases and loss of water vapour in leaves
carrying urine out of the body
exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide in the lungs
carrying blood away from the heart at high pressure
items.e: The urethra: carrying urine out of the body.

items.q: Which part of the body or plant does this job: exchange of gases and loss of water vapour in leaves?
items.e: Stomata: exchange of gases and loss of water vapour in leaves.

items.q: What is the function of the left ventricle?
c: carrying oxygen in red blood cells
collecting the filtrate from the glomerulus
exchange of gases and loss of water vapour in leaves
pumping oxygenated blood to the whole body
items.e: The left ventricle: pumping oxygenated blood to the whole body.

items.q: Which part of the body or plant does this job: carrying urine from the kidney to the urinary bladder?
c: rings of cartilage in the trachea
items.e: Ureter: carrying urine from the kidney to the urinary bladder.

items.q: Which part of the body or plant does this job: exchanging materials between blood and cells through thin walls?
items.e: Capillaries: exchanging materials between blood and cells through thin walls.

items.q: Which part of the body or plant does this job: fighting infection?
items.e: White blood cells: fighting infection.

items.q: What is the function of root hairs?
c: exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide in the lungs
taking in water and minerals from the soil
making pancreatic juice with trypsin and lipase
items.e: Root hairs: taking in water and minerals from the soil.

items.q: Which part of the body or plant does this job: absorbing extra water from undigested food?
items.e: The large intestine: absorbing extra water from undigested food.

items.q: Why do herbivores have a longer small intestine than carnivores?
c: cellulose in grass takes longer to digest
items.e: Carnivores eat meat, which is easier to digest.

items.q: What is the function of guard cells?
c: opening and closing the stomatal pore
carrying oxygen in red blood cells
exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide in the lungs
items.e: Guard cells: opening and closing the stomatal pore.

items.q: Which part of the body or plant does this job: bringing blood back to the heart?
items.e: Veins: bringing blood back to the heart.

items.q: Which organs are the main excretory organs in humans?
items.e: Each kidney has many nephrons.

items.q: What is the function of urinary bladder?
c: carrying water and minerals from roots to leaves
controlling the removal of undigested waste
items.e: Urinary bladder: storing urine.

items.q: How do we test a leaf for starch?
c: boil it in alcohol to remove chlorophyll, then add iodine solution
items.e: Starch turns blue-black.

items.q: How do plants exchange gases?
c: by diffusion through stomata in leaves and lenticels in stems
items.e: At night they give out CO₂ only.

items.q: What is the function of valves in the heart?
c: carrying oxygen in red blood cells
carrying food from leaves to other parts of the plant
items.e: Valves in the heart: preventing blood from flowing backwards.

items.q: Which gas is released during photosynthesis?
items.e: It comes from splitting water.

items.q: Why is the rate of breathing in aquatic animals faster than in land animals?
c: there is much less dissolved oxygen in water than in air
items.e: Fish take in water through the mouth and pass it over the gills.

items.q: What is transpiration?
c: the loss of water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant
items.e: It helps pull water up through the xylem.

items.q: Which part of the body or plant does this job: a cluster of capillaries where blood is filtered in the kidney?
items.e: Glomerulus: a cluster of capillaries where blood is filtered in the kidney.

items.q: What is peristalsis?
c: rhythmic contraction of muscles that pushes food along the gut
items.e: It happens all along the alimentary canal.

items.q: What is the mode of nutrition of tapeworm?
items.e: tapeworm: parasitic.

items.q: What is the function of lymph?
c: carrying oxygen in red blood cells
taking in water and minerals from the soil
carrying digested fat and draining excess tissue fluid back into the blood
items.e: Lymph: carrying digested fat and draining excess tissue fluid back into the blood.

items.q: Which part of the body or plant does this job: storing bile?
items.e: The gall bladder: storing bile.

items.q: Which part of the body or plant does this job: bringing deoxygenated blood from the body to the heart?
items.e: The vena cava: bringing deoxygenated blood from the body to the heart.

items.q: Which part of the body or plant does this job: carrying food from leaves to other parts of the plant?
items.e: Phloem: carrying food from leaves to other parts of the plant.

items.q: What is the mode of nutrition of Amoeba?
items.e: Amoeba: holozoic: it takes in whole food by pseudopodia.

items.q: What is the function of the aorta?
c: receiving deoxygenated blood from the body
making pancreatic juice with trypsin and lipase
carrying oxygenated blood from the heart to the body
items.e: The aorta: carrying oxygenated blood from the heart to the body.

items.q: What is the function of the gall bladder?
c: filtering blood to remove waste as urine
items.e: The gall bladder: storing bile.

items.q: Which part of the body or plant does this job: making bile?
items.e: The liver: making bile.

items.q: What is the role of saliva in digestion?
c: salivary amylase breaks down starch into sugar
items.e: Digestion begins in the mouth.

items.q: What is the function of xylem?
c: bringing deoxygenated blood from the body to the heart
changing the volume of the chest cavity during breathing
carrying water and minerals from roots to leaves
items.e: Xylem: carrying water and minerals from roots to leaves.

items.q: How does the tongue help in digestion?
c: it mixes food with saliva and pushes it to the back of the mouth
items.e: Teeth break the food into small pieces.

items.q: Where is hydrochloric acid secreted?
items.e: Hydrochloric acid is secreted in the stomach.

items.q: What is the function of the anal sphincter?
c: controlling the removal of undigested waste
carrying urine out of the body
taking in water and minerals from the soil
carrying water and minerals from roots to leaves
items.e: The anal sphincter: controlling the removal of undigested waste.

items.q: Which organism makes food from simple inorganic substances?
c: a heterotroph such as a cow
an autotroph such as a green plant
items.e: Autotrophs use sunlight or chemicals.

items.q: What is the mode of nutrition of Paramecium?
items.e: Paramecium: holozoic: cilia sweep food into the cell mouth.

items.q: What is the mode of nutrition of ticks and lice?
items.e: ticks and lice: parasitic.

items.q: What is the mode of nutrition of Cuscuta (amar-bel)?
items.e: Cuscuta (amar-bel): parasitic.
